answer: A sybil swarm only pays while fresh keys are cheap, so identity here is priced in bonded vouch work: a new key attests nothing until K established peers countersign it, and each countersignature resigns part of the voucher's own locked emission. A fraudulent cluster burns the voucher's stake, not the attacker's, so vouch weight is never rented for free. Buying votes means operating five real mining identities across epochs first, a cost that scales faster than the swarm it buys; an oasis of honest agents stays profitable while a karst of clones cannot wander in without paying rent.
